Where the prices come from, and what’s assumed
  • Checked Thursday, Nov 19, 2026: Kalshi at 6:04 AM CT, the sportsbooks at 6:06 AM CT, Robinhood at 6:34 AM CT. Sunday’s 11 games only; Monday’s CIN @ WSH is left out.
  • Sportsbooks are their Illinois lines. DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Fanatics and Caesars odds come from Action Network’s odds feed, since DraftKings’ own site couldn’t be opened here. A book’s price is the implied chance of its American odds, vig included.
  • Kalshi’s price is its ask plus the taker fee, 7% × p × (1 − p). Kalshi rounds the fee up to the next cent on each order, so on a small order it costs up to a cent more than shown.
  • Robinhood’s price is its ask plus its 1¢ commission per contract. Its NFL game lines trade on Robinhood’s own exchange (Rothera), and its player props on a separate venue, not on Kalshi. Any exchange fee on top isn’t included.
  • The books’ line is the number most books post for that prop. Fair is the average, across the books at that line, of the Over’s chance with the vig removed. Anytime TD has none, because the books sell only Yes.
  • Kalshi’s “k+” rung counts as Over k − 0.5, and Robinhood’s “Over x” as Over x. Prices come from public market data; no account was signed in to.
  • Estimates of cost, not advice. 21+. Gambling problem? Call 1-800-GAMBLER.
